related_questions.question: What is the Schedule A on a tax return?
related_questions.snippet: For individual taxpayers, Schedule A is used in conjunction with Form 1040 to report itemized deductions. If you choose to claim itemized deductions instead of the standard deduction, you would use Schedule A to list your deductions. Your itemized total is then subtracted from your taxable income.

related_questions.question: Can you deduct state income tax on Schedule A?
related_questions.snippet: As an individual, your deduction for state and local taxes (SALT) (lines 5a, 5b and 5c on Schedule A of Form 1040) is limited to a combined total deduction of $10,000 ($5,000 if married filing separately). You may be subject to a limit on some of your other itemized deductions also.
